key_insight: Neural networks applied to text embeddings can reliably quantify levels of peace from news and generalize across different news datasets; similar ML-driven analyses and user-facing tools can help people understand and improve their media diets to foster peace.
problem_solved: Provides a scalable, automated way to measure 'levels of peace' from news and social media and addresses the gap in tools that give users actionable insight into how their media consumption affects peace-related signals.
method: Train neural-network classifiers/regressors on text embeddings derived from online news sources to produce a continuous 'peace' score; validate cross-dataset generalization (high accuracy when applied to a different news dataset).
Apply platform-specific embedding and feature extraction techniques to social media (e.g., YouTube) to capture peace-related signals from user-generated content and engagement patterns.
Develop online, user-facing tools that visualize individual media diets and provide recommendations to promote more peace-positive consumption patterns.
impact: Enables ML/AI practitioners to build robust, cross-domain peace metrics and practical interventions for media literacy and policy monitoring; demonstrates a path for combining NLP, cross-dataset validation, and user tools in ML-for-good applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data sources → embeddings → neural model → peace score
World map heatmap showing country-level peace scores derived from news
Before/after user dashboard mockup displaying a user's media diet and suggested changes
Bar/line chart comparing model performance on training vs. independent news datasets (generalization)
paper_title: Measuring and Fostering Peace through Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence
paper_authors: P. Gilda, P. Dungarwal, A. Thongkham, E. T. Ajayi, S. Choudhary
